witnesses.title: Cod. Guelf. 47.13 Aug. 4°: Book of Abramelin
witnesses.dateNotes: The repository catalog dates the paper manuscript to the seventeenth century. The text's internal claim of 1438 is not used as the witness date.
witnesses.completeness: The Abramelin work occupies ff. 1–31v; the remainder contains Jewish prayers and a register.
witnesses.provenance: The catalog records a 1775 loan to Duke Friedrich August of Brunswick-Oels and return from the Berlin state archive in 1858.
witnesses.rights: Catalog metadata public; physical and reproduction access governed by the Herzog August Bibliothek.
witnesses.description: A repository-cataloged seventeenth-century German manuscript witness. Atlas keeps its physical date separate from the narrative date claimed by the work.

witnesses.title: Sloane MS 3648: Lesser Key of Solomon (Lemegeton)
witnesses.dateNotes: The repository catalogs ff. 1–47 as the French Lesser Key of Solomon (Lemegeton), dated 1572, within a manuscript whose other contents extend through the seventeenth century.
witnesses.completeness: The catalog identifies the Lemegeton section at ff. 1–47; Atlas does not infer that it contains every later standardized subdivision.
witnesses.provenance: Sloane Collection; no earlier ownership chain is asserted here.
witnesses.rights: Catalog metadata public; physical and reproduction access governed by the British Library.
witnesses.description: A repository-cataloged physical witness for the Lemegeton. The five conventional book records cite this catalog but are not each claimed as separately cataloged sections.

witnesses.title: Sloane MS 3825: Clavicle of Solomon and magical miscellany
witnesses.dateNotes: The catalog identifies the French Clavicle of Solomon at ff. 100–179 as 1572 and other magical texts as seventeenth century; these dates describe contents in this physical volume.
witnesses.completeness: Composite manuscript; not a complete witness to every Solomonic work
witnesses.provenance: Owned by John Somers and Sir Joseph Jekyll; acquired from Jekyll's 1739/40 sale, according to the British Library catalog.
witnesses.rights: Catalog metadata public; physical and reproduction access governed by the British Library.
witnesses.description: A real physical witness linked only to the Key of Solomon material explicitly identified by the repository. It is not asserted as a Lemegeton witness.

witnesses.title: Yates Thompson MS 36: Dante, Divina commedia
witnesses.dateNotes: British Library catalog: made in Tuscany after 1444, conventionally dated to about 1444–1450; the date describes this witness, not Dante's composition.
witnesses.completeness: Inferno, Purgatorio, and Paradiso in one volume
witnesses.provenance: Recorded at San Miguel de los Reyes, Valencia, in 1613; bought by Henry Yates Thompson in 1901 and bequeathed to the British Museum in 1941.
witnesses.rights: British Library catalog and digitized-content terms apply.
witnesses.description: A repository-cataloged physical manuscript of all three cantiche, kept distinct from the bundled Longfellow translation.

witnesses.title: Malleus maleficarum, Nuremberg 1494
witnesses.dateNotes: Printed at Nuremberg by Anton Koberger in 1494, according to the institutional catalog.
witnesses.provenance: Institutional holding metadata; no earlier ownership chain is asserted here.
witnesses.rights: Catalog metadata public; item access and reproduction follow Wellcome Collection terms.
witnesses.description: A dated physical copy that supports print-history research. Its claims about witchcraft are historical allegations, not verified evidence of supernatural acts.
